Rome fell in the West in 476 AD.

It never stopped being claimed.

France, Germany, Russia, Turkey, even Mussolini's Italy — all at some point insisted THEY were Rome's true heir.

Who actually had a case — a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The strongest claim barely needed reinventing. The Eastern Roman Empire never fell in 476 — it just kept going from Constantinople, calling itself Rome for another 977 years, until 1453.
2/ The West wanted it back badly. Christmas Day, 800 AD: the Pope crowns the Frankish king Charlemagne 'Emperor of the Romans' — reviving a title that had sat empty for 300+ years.
3/ That fiction became the Holy Roman Empire in 962. Voltaire later joked it was neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire — it still ran Central Europe for 844 years.
4/ When Constantinople actually fell in 1453, the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II immediately titled himself 'Kayser-i Rum' — Caesar of Rome. Rules were: whoever holds the capital, holds the crown.

5/ Moscow disagreed. A monk told the Russian tsar around 1510 that Rome fell once to heresy, once to the Turks — and Moscow was the 'Third Rome.' The word 'tsar' is literally a contraction of 'Caesar.'

6/ Napoleon followed the same 1,000-year-old playbook in 1804: Roman eagles, a Senate on classical lines, a self-coronation timed almost exactly 1,004 years after Charlemagne's.

Which claim do you buy? Full story: https://buttondown.com/forummapping
